toni: Quick flag - ran into a parity/formatting issue between our Node SDK batching helper and the Python SDK while testing the retriever sample app. Node ended up truncating vectors to the shortest in the batch, Python errored on mismatch. Result: rerank returned garbage scores for a few queries.

lena: oof. truncating? can you share a tiny repro payload and which helper version?

toni: using @redwood/sdk-js v1.4.2 Batcher. repro (simplified):
```json
{"inputs": [[0.01,0.02,0.03,...(512 values)...], [0.05,0.06,...(768 values)...]]}
```
Node request body that hit the server looked like second vector trimmed to 512 values instead of 768. Python threw an error before sending.

patrick: interesting - is the trim happening in serialization (typedarray -> JSON) or in the helper merge step? Any client-side logs?

toni: traced it to the packer in the batch helper. When it detects mixed typed arrays it currently coerces to the shortest length to keep a rectangular shape for our internal buffer. That was intended for some legacy numeric pipelines but it's absolutely unsafe for semantic vectors.

lena: agreed this is dangerous. We should never silently modify vector semantics. Short-term: change behavior to fail loudly when mixed lengths are observed, and include the offending index in the error. Long-term: add strict shape validation that compares to model_dim.

sdk-ci: Note: failing loudly will be a behavior change. flagging for changelog and SDK semver policy.

toni: suggestion: 1) default -> throw on mixed lengths, 2) provide an explicit opt-in pad/truncate flag (pad_with=NaN|0|truncate) behind a config option, 3) surface model_dim in model metadata so SDK can auto-validate.

patrick: +1. also add a runtime check in the retriever example so app devs hit the error before they deploy. e.g., simple assert in wrapper: 
```js
if (vec.length !== modelDim) throw new Error(`Expected ${modelDim}, got ${vec.length} for id ${id}`)
```

lena: I'll open a PR for the helper change and add unit tests that run the same test against Node and Python to ensure parity. Also adding a telemetry event 'embed.shape.mismatch' with counts so we can find impacted customers.

sdk-ci: CI job queued for pr #542 - tests include new cross-sdk parity suite.

toni: For support: I'll draft a migration note showing how to enable pad/truncate for customers who relied on old behavior, and a small script for scanning logs for embed.shape.mismatch events.

patrick: ops note - when we flip default to fail, add a feature flag in Dedicated/Private to let customers opt into old behavior for a rollout window.

lena: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/542 - changes summary in PR description. added integration test against the retriever example.

sdk-ci: Integration tests passed for pr #542. Merge scheduled to next minor release.

toni: thanks all. leaving this thread pinned. I'll send the support doc to #support once draft is ready. :thumbsup:
